title: Kryptos K4
caveat: Progress here means ruling cipher models out against the artist's disclosed clues, fitting one clue and holding the other back. The plaintext is reported to sit in a private archive sold in November 2025, and the custodian still lists K4 as unsolved; the question here is a public method, not whether anyone knows the answer. The share is of the families listed, not of every cipher.

lay.tagline: The last unsolved panel of a sculpture outside CIA headquarters.
lay.summary: Kryptos is a sculpture unveiled at CIA headquarters in 1990. Three of its four enciphered panels were read in the 1990s; the fourth, 97 letters long, has never been publicly solved. The artist has released a few words of the answer and where they sit. We use one of those clues to fit a cipher and keep the other back to check it, so a cipher that only fits by luck is caught.
lay.what_it_is: K4 is 97 capital letters on a copper sheet. Jim Sanborn, the artist, has said that the letters at certain positions spell EASTNORTHEAST and BERLINCLOCK. Any proposed method must turn the 97 letters into a text with those words in exactly those places.
lay.what_we_found: Every cipher model we searched to completion either cannot place the clues at all or, when its key is fully pinned down by one clue, gets the other clue wrong. 888 complete keys from layered Vigenere, autokey and Beaufort models with column shuffles all failed the held-back clue. Some partial keys are still undecided.
lay.whats_next: Only add a new cipher model when there is a reason the artist could have used it, fix the clue positions before fitting, and keep one clue for checking. The artist's archive and the custodian's answer checker are private; a matching answer from them would be a reference, not a method.

faq.a: Not publicly. An archive with the plaintext was auctioned in November 2025, and the new custodian runs a private answer checker, but no full method has been published in the sources we checked.

faq.q: Why not just try every cipher?
faq.a: With only 97 letters, many wrong keys can produce a few English-looking words. Holding one clue back is how we tell a real fit from a lucky one.

researcher.summary: 97-letter K4 (ASCII SHA-256 eea81357...). Clues fitted and reserved in reciprocal folds: EASTNORTHEAST at zero-based plaintext offset 21 and BERLINCLOCK at 63. A reserved exact prediction requires a complete key and every reserved letter equal. Completed spaces: ragged columnar (widths to 32, both read orders, A-Z and KRYPTOS alphabets) composed either side of repeating, plaintext-autokey, ciphertext-autokey and Beaufort substitution at periods to 32 (65,024 hypotheses), 0 reserved exact predictions.

charts.title: What happened to 65,024 layered cipher hypotheses
charts.caption: Ragged columnar transposition composed with repeating, autokey and Beaufort substitution, both clue folds. A reserved exact prediction would need a complete key that spells the held-back clue.

statuses.excluded-by-constraint: Excluded by the clues: every complete key the model allows contradicts a disclosed clue held back from fitting, or the model cannot place the clues at all.
statuses.tested-without-power: Tested, not closed: the search ran, but some hypotheses stay underdetermined, the budget ran out, or matched-length controls did not come back.
statuses.excluded-by-count: Excluded by a count: a measured statistic falls outside a threshold fixed before K4 was scored and checked on planted controls. This is statistical, not exact.
statuses.open: Open: not searched here, or not searched with a method shown to work.

families.family: Ragged columnar transposition with repeating, autokey or Beaufort substitution, either order, periods and widths to 32
families.evidence: All 65,024 hypotheses of both folds were checked; 888 have complete keys and all 888 contradict the held-back clue, but 2,563 stay undetermined and no planted-text control at 97 letters is recorded.

families.family: Progressive key on a straight alphabet, periods 1 to 32
families.evidence: 832 settings in each fold; every fully determined candidate fails the held-back phrase, and partial keys remain underdetermined.

families.family: Reversal or rotation followed by affine substitution
families.evidence: 5,000 hypotheses in each fold returned no candidate and stopped at the check limit, so the space is not finished.

families.family: In-place Quagmire, progressive and autokey forms on unknown alphabets at the periods and lags the clues do not block
families.evidence: For the 137 such settings up to 32, fitting one clue forces 8 of 3,288 held-back letters (all right) and leaves 3,280 free, so the clues cannot test these settings.

families.family: The same transpositions with any alphabet in each column, periods 3 to 26
families.evidence: The bijection bound excludes periods 1 and 2 everywhere and period 3 when substitution comes first; at higher periods it removes about the share it removes from planted wrong hypotheses, so the survivors are what chance leaves. Complete keys exist only at periods 21 to 24 and test at most 3 clue letters.

families.family: In-place Hill 6 by 6 to 10 by 10, and Hill 5 by 5 at 6 settings
families.evidence: Every row fits and an invertible fit exists, and fitting one clue forces no letter of the other, so the clues cannot test these sizes; listing the keys (1.4e14 to beyond 1e140) is out of reach.

families.family: In-place periodic substitution with any alphabets (any Quagmire keyword, keyed Vigenere, Beaufort, Porta) at periods 1-7, 9, 10, 14, 15, 17, 21, 25
families.evidence: In one column the same plaintext letter would need two ciphertext letters, or two plaintext letters one ciphertext letter, for any alphabets. Periods 8, 11-13, 16, 18-20, 22-24 and 26-32 are not blocked by this bound; a planted-clue control is never blocked.

families.family: Pure columnar transposition in complete rectangles
families.evidence: 97 is prime, so no complete rectangle of width 2 to 32 exists; ragged rectangles are the family above.

families.family: Condi with 20 guessed keywords
families.evidence: 13,520 settings in each fold produced no candidate that fits the training clue.

families.family: In-place ACA Gromark with digits 0 to 9, any keyword, and Myszkowski under KRYPTOS, PALIMPSEST or ABSCISSA on either side
families.evidence: Ciphertext letters F, K and P cannot share one alphabet index with both clues, for any keyword or primer; a control with both clues planted is not blocked.

families.family: Quagmire I to IV with the three published keywords
families.evidence: 11,310 settings decrypted; none places a clue.

families.family: Porta, Playfair, two-square and periodic Gromark with the three published keywords
families.evidence: Porta and periodic Gromark place neither clue; Playfair and two-square cannot take an odd length without a pad the sculpture does not show.

families.family: Running key from the K3 plaintext, and 2 by 2 Hill
families.evidence: 240 K3 offsets place no clue; 2 by 2 Hill on either 96-letter window has no inverse row that fits the training clue, in both folds.

families.family: In-place keyed Vigenere (Quagmire III, the K1 and K2 system) with any alphabet and keyword at every period 1 to 26, and other Quagmire, progressive and autokey forms on unknown alphabets at the periods and lags listed in the log
families.evidence: An exact Z3 check of both clues, with every alphabet left free, is unsatisfiable at those periods and lags across ten families; no language model is used, so it holds whatever language the rest of K4 is in. A control with both clues planted under each family is never blocked.

families.family: In-place Hill, 2 by 2 to 4 by 4, every block alignment, letters numbered A to Z, KRYPTOS, PALIMPSEST or ABSCISSA
families.evidence: Every one of the 26^n candidate decryption rows was tried. At 2 by 2 and 3 by 3 no row fits both clues; at 4 by 4 no fitting rows form a matrix invertible mod 26. Planted controls are never excluded, and at 3 by 3 one clue pins all of the other under a planted key.

families.family: Every column order to width 10, K3-style double rotation, route reads and keyword orders, composed either way with straight or KRYPTOS-keyed Vigenere or Beaufort at periods 1 to 20, on 97 letters or 98 with the K3 question mark
families.evidence: 855,465,832 hypotheses in all; no hypothesis at periods 1 to 20 lets one shift per column place both clues. The C kernel matches the Python reference, the family code reproduces K3 from its plaintext, and 200 planted controls per family are never excluded.

families.family: Running keys from 19 frozen texts (K1 to K3 plaintext and ciphertext, Carter's Tutankhamun volumes, the King James Bible, the Declaration and Constitution, English and German novels) under Vigenere, Beaufort and variant Beaufort on A-Z, KRYPTOS, PALIMPSEST or ABSCISSA, read either way
families.evidence: No offset in any text places all 24 clue key letters under any of the 12 tableaux; the best partial matches (3 to 9 of 24) are what chance gives. Planted keys are found at the right offset.

families.family: In-place Hill 5 by 5 at 11 of its 20 alignment and numbering settings
families.evidence: Solving each row mod 2 and mod 13 shows that some row cannot fit both clues or that no fitting rows form a matrix invertible mod 26; the row counts match brute force over all 26^5 rows, and planted keys are never excluded.

families.family: In-place keyed Vigenere with any alphabet even if one clue letter is wrong (a misspelling like those in K1 to K3), periods 1 to 18, 20 to 22 and 25
families.evidence: MaxSAT shows K4 needs at least two dropped clue letters at those periods; random strings need about as many or fewer, and 208 family and period settings show nothing significant (period 19 fits 1 to 4 percent of random strings).

families.family: Two repeating keys added on one keyed alphabet: 37 Vigenere-sense and 31 Beaufort-sense length pairs whose combined cycle exceeds 26
families.evidence: Exact SAT with the alphabet left free; every pair of lengths 2 to 26 was checked and planted controls always fit.

families.family: Every column order at widths 11 to 16, composed either way with straight or KRYPTOS-keyed Vigenere or Beaufort, at periods 1 to 16 (widths 11 to 14), 1 to 15 (width 15) and 1 to 14 (width 16), on 97 or 98 letters
families.evidence: Branch and bound (widths 11 to 13) and a SAT model (14 to 16) find no fitting order; both agree with the full enumeration where it can run, and planted keys are found. Orders that fit at longer periods decrypt to random-like text.

families.family: Any English-prose running key, in place, under those 12 tableaux
families.evidence: The two clue fragments of the key score at the 0.0000 percentile of 1,916,325 aligned English fragment pairs under every tableau, read either way; none of 7,981 planted clean-prose keys scores as low as K4's best.

families.family: In-place Hill 5 by 5 at the 3 settings small enough to list in full, for English plaintext
families.evidence: All 26^5 clue-consistent keys per setting were decrypted; the best K4 quadgram score (-4.77 a quadgram) is far below the worst of 239 English windows (-2.67) and inside the range random text reaches. Planted English keys come first in 88 of 90 controls.

families.family: Keyed alphabets other than A to Z and KRYPTOS, under the layered models
families.evidence: The layered space used two alphabets only. In place, unknown alphabets are now checked exactly, so the open question is unknown alphabets combined with a transposition.
families.next: Add unknown Quagmire-style alphabets to the layered search with the optional symbolic engine, clue positions frozen before fitting and one clue held back.

families.family: Column orders of width 17 and above, longer periods at widths 11 to 16, double columnar, grilles and other transpositions combined with substitution
families.evidence: Every column order to width 16 is done for Vigenere and Beaufort on A-Z and KRYPTOS at periods up to 14 to 16; a widths 17 to 24 SAT run was stopped unfinished.
families.next: Finish widths 17 to 24 with engine.k4_columnar_sat (a few CPU hours, splittable), then double columnar with a stated construction reason, with planted controls.

families.family: Running keys that are not English prose or not in the frozen list
families.evidence: 19 frozen texts are excluded exactly and English prose statistically; other languages, lists and non-prose keys are not.
families.next: Add sourced non-English key texts with hashes before any search, with planted keys as controls.

families.family: Fractionating ciphers (bifid, trifid) and Gromark variants beyond the ACA digit rule
families.evidence: A calibrated neural family prior trained on planted 97-letter ciphertexts puts K4 with random letters (0.36), Gromark (0.32) and trifid (0.12), and far from short periods, autokey, running key, Hill and pure transposition. A prior is a search order, not evidence of a method.
families.next: Write clue-only checks for in-place bifid and trifid with unknown squares and for Gromark with other digit rules, with planted controls, before any language-scored search.
